info.name: RallyDeals - Catalog Service
info.description:
# RallyDeals Catalog Service

Test collection for the catalog service, routed **through the API Gateway** (`http://localhost:8080`). The gateway must be running with `CATALOG_SERVICE_URI` pointing at the catalog service (`http://localhost:8083`).

## Authentication

Every request below sends `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`. The gateway **parses and validates** the JWT (rally-common `JwtService.parseAndValidate`; JWT is signed HMAC, not encrypted), strips it, and **injects identity headers** before forwarding:

- `X-User-Id`  -> value of the JWT `sub` claim
- `X-User-Role` -> value of the JWT roles claim

The catalog service never validates the token itself; it reads `X-User-Id` / `X-User-Role` and trusts them (they come only from the gateway).

The collection ships with **pre-generated static dev tokens** (expire 2099) in the `sellerJwt` / `buyerJwt` / `adminJwt` collection variables, signed with the canonical dev `JWT_SECRET`: `/Wepykoli0z1033egoGDdLrm3eohJiOJUxT5L/RxgV0=`. They work against the locally running gateway with no Auth Service up. To regenerate, sign an HS256 JWT with that secret, matching the `sub`/`iss`/`roles` shape `JwtService` expects:

- `sellerJwt` -> sub `11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111` (a UUID, since the catalog reads `X-User-Id` as a UUID), roles `["SELLER"]`
- `buyerJwt`  -> sub `22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222`, roles `["BUYER"]`
- `adminJwt`  -> sub `33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333`, roles `["ADMIN"]`
- `iss` = `rally-auth-service`, plus `iat`/`exp`

> **Note:** if you get 401s, the gateway process is running with a *different* `JWT_SECRET` than this canonical value. Restart it so it re-reads `rally-gateway/.env`.

## Seed data

Run the requests in order: the **Categories -> Create Category** and **Products -> Create Product** requests save their generated ids into the `categoryId` / `productId` collection variables, so later requests run end-to-end.

## Notes

- The tokens' `sub` must match the `sellerId` (`user-1`) and `buyerId` (`user-2`) collection variables Ã¢â‚¬â€ the create-product assertion checks `sellerId` equals `user-1`.
- `GET /products/{id}` returns `404` for buyers/non-owners and `200` for the owning seller, `ADMIN`, or when called with an admin token.
- `GET /products` (buyer view) only returns `APPROVED` and non-deleted products.
- `GET /products/sellers/{sellerId}` and `GET /products/admin` include soft-deleted products by default (`includeDeleted` defaults to `true`); responses expose `deleted` / `deletedAt` so you can tell them apart.
- Admin queue lives at `/products/admin` (see Admin Moderation folder).

item.name: Categories
item.description: Category taxonomy CRUD. In production, write operations go through the gateway as an admin; these requests send an admin JWT (`{{adminJwt}}`).

item.name: Products
item.description: Product lifecycle. `X-User-Id` is taken from the gateway-injected header (derived from the JWT), never from the request body (see `deal-service.md` Ã‚Â§4.2 for the same rule).

exec: pm.test("paginated response shape", () => { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j).to.have.property('items'); pm.expect(j).to.have.property('total'); });

pm.test("re-delete -> 410 Gone", () => { pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.request.url.toString(), method: 'DELETE', header: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('sellerJwt') } }, (e, r) => pm.expect(r.code).to.eql(410)); });
pm.test("items expose deleted state", () => { const j = pm.response.json(); for (const it of j.items) { pm.expect(it).to.have.property('deleted'); pm.expect(it).to.have.property('deletedAt'); } });
pm.test("found/notFound split", () => { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j).to.have.property('found'); pm.expect(j).to.have.property('notFound'); });
